summary.text: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is totally consumed when a chemical reaction is completed.
The amount of product formed is limited by it, since the reaction cannot continue without it, and reagents present beyond what is needed are called excess reagents.
It must be identified to calculate percentage yield, because the theoretical yield is the amount of product obtained when it reacts completely.

facts.label: Leftover reagents
facts.value: Called excess reagents, excess reactants, or in abundance

facts.label: Why it matters
facts.value: Needed to calculate a reaction's percentage yield

facts.label: Product-based method
facts.value: The limiting reactant forms the smallest amount of product

facts.label: Two-reactant method
facts.value: Most useful when there are only two reactants

items.prompt: A lab report says a reaction stopped because it could not continue without reactant X. How should X be described?

options.label: Totally used up, capping how much product forms
Present in excess, with plenty left over at the end
A product that was formed in an earlier step
Not involved in the reaction in any way

items.explain: The limiting reagent is totally consumed when the reaction is completed, and the product formed is limited by it.

items.prompt: A mixture of Al and Fe₂O₃ could make 0.297 mol Fe from the Al but only 0.250 mol Fe from the Fe₂O₃. How much Fe can actually form?

options.label: 0.297 mol, set by the larger amount
0.250 mol, set by the smaller amount
0.547 mol, the two amounts added
0.047 mol, the gap between them

items.explain: The limiting reactant is the one that can form the smallest amount of product, so the iron produced is limited to 0.250 mol.

items.prompt: A student wants to express how well her experiment did as a percentage of the best possible result. What must she pin down first?

options.label: Which reactant is the cheapest to buy and to replace
Which product is the heaviest once it has been collected
Which reactant is limiting, as it sets the theoretical yield
Which reactant was poured in first, since it reacts first

items.explain: The limiting reagent must be identified to calculate percentage yield, since the theoretical yield is the product obtained when the limiting reagent reacts completely.

items.prompt: You pick reactant A and work out how much of reactant B it needs. The flask holds more B than that. Which reactant limits the reaction?

options.label: B, since there is more of it
B, since it was worked out second
Neither, since both are in abundance
A, since B is present in excess

items.explain: If the amount of B present exceeds the amount required, B is in excess and A is the limiting reagent.

items.prompt: Two reactants are each checked for how much of the same product they could form. Which one is limiting?

options.label: The one that could form the least product
The one that could form the most product
The one present in the larger mass
The one written first in the equation

items.explain: The limiting reactant is the one which can form the smallest amount of the product considered.

items.prompt: A chemist runs a reaction until it can go no further. One reagent was present beyond what the other required. What is true of that surplus afterwards?

options.label: All of it is used up with the other
It turns into extra product beyond the limit
Some of it is left over, unreacted
It changes into the other reagent

items.explain: Reagents present in excess of what the limiting reagent needs are left over; in the example, 6.75 mol of oxygen remains unreacted.
